title: feat(world,mesh): Mesh extraction from voxel SDF — fast-surface-nets primary + custom DC follow-up
abstract:
> **2026-10-28:** part of #313 (planets), under #397 (volumetric layer).

Preservar SDF como autoring tool extrayendo mesh para render.

## Approach

- Dual Contouring sobre voxel grid sparse (octree de SDF samples)
- Hermite data en cada cell (intersection + normal)
- QEF solver para vertex placement preciso en aristas
- Output: meshlet-compatible buffers (vértices + índices) listos para Phase 1 pipeline

## Cuándo

Phase 2 del roadmap, post mesh GPU-driven pipeline operativa.

## Por qué importa

Preserva la identidad SDF del engine. Autoría sigue siendo CSG suave + brushes; runtime extrae mesh y lo renderiza con la pipeline state-of-the-art.

## Referencias

- Nick's Voxel Blog: Implementing Dual Contouring
- dexyfex.com: Voxels and Dual Contouring
- Dual Universe (proven shipped product con dual contouring)
- `godot_voxel` (Zylann, MIT, github.com/Zylann/godot_voxel) — implementación de referencia
  con mesher de LOD (Transvoxel) en producción; útil para el diseño de QEF solver, manejo de
  Hermite data y transition cells entre niveles de LOD aunque el algoritmo base difiera
  (ver nota de diseño en el epic #397).

Ver `docs/research/stack_decisions_2026-05-02.md`.

## Nota (2026-09-05)

El título de esta issue ("fast-surface-nets primary + custom DC follow-up") quedó desalineado
con #614 Finding 2: para LOD sobre octree, Dual Contouring es crack-free por construcción y
Marching Cubes/Surface Nets necesita Transvoxel para lo mismo que DC no tiene que resolver.
Sigue habiendo un caso de uso real para Surface Nets (más simple, sin QEF, cuando no hace
falta preservar features/esquinas ni LOD por octree) — si esta issue se separa en dos
(extracción simple vs. extracción con LOD), hacerlo como issues nuevas en vez de forzarlo
acá. Por ahora el approach de arriba (DC puro) es el que aplica al pipeline planet-scale de
#397/#313/#614.



## Research (2026-11-22)
Capability: dual contouring (Hermite data + QEF vertex) of GPU-generated SDF blocks on an LOD octree, with crack-free seams between blocks of different level. Trigger: surface nets seams in #1979 (measured there) — the user chose to replace the mesher instead of patching it.
Searched: crates.io/lib.rs (dual contouring, QEF, isosurface), GitHub (GPU DC, chunked DC LOD seams), Gildea's blog, Zylann docs.
Candidates:
- `fidget-mesh` — manifold DC on an octree, CPU, built from a whole shape: no per-block GPU path. Study only.
- `dual_contouring` (soundeffects) — CPU, uniform grid, no LOD. Rejected as a dep.
- `isosurface`, `fast-surface-nets` — MC / surface nets, not DC. Rejected.
- Gildea, *Dual contouring: chunked terrain* + *Engine overview* (Leven): chunk meshes plus a **seam mesh per chunk built from the border nodes of the chunk and its neighbours at any LOD**, cloned into a temporary octree and contoured. The reference design for chunked DC.
- `proton2/java-leven` — Java/OpenCL port of Leven with LOD seams, holes in seams fixed. Read for the seam selection.
- `Olaxan/dual-deserts`, `Tuntenfisch/Voxels` — GPU compute DC: QEF with a centre bias (Olaxan) or Schmitz particles instead of the QEF (Tuntenfisch). Read for the GPU vertex solve.
**Verdict: STUDY** — no crate meshes GPU blocks; copy Leven's seam design and a GPU QEF (centre-biased, Schaefer–Warren QR or Schmitz particles). Reading only, no code copied.

## Design (as built, 2026-11-23)
1. **Vertex** (`nets.wgsl` `place`): DC. Edge crossings + trilinear gradient of the tile → one-pass QEF per cell (AᵀA, Aᵀb, mass point), centre-biased (λ = 0.05), solved by adjugate, clamped to the cell. No per-thread arrays, so no scratch memory (#1938). A cell with no crossing keeps the old Newton step.
2. **2:1 balance** (`select.rs`): splitting a leaf first splits every coarser leaf touching it, so touching leaves are never more than one level apart. Pinned by `touching_leaves_are_balanced`.
3. **Transactional swap** (`draw/swap.rs`, `draw/agree.rs`): the cracks measured in #1979 were a timing bug, not a mesh bug. A block already on screen took its re-mesh at once, while the new neighbour it was meshed against waited hidden. Now every mesh is staged. Each frame, the swap shows a set of staged meshes only when nothing lingering overlaps them and every one agrees with its neighbours' `Near` (same level: both `OWN`; coarser: the finer one borrows that slot, the coarser one says `FINER`). Holding one back can hold others, so the set shrinks to a fixed point (≤ 8 passes) and goes on screen in one frame. `LINGER` (240 frames) bounds any wait.
4. **Bit-identical shared samples** (`generate.wgsl`, `Job::new`): altitude was computed from each tile's own corner, so two blocks could store a shared sample one f16 ulp apart. It is now computed from an anchor fixed on the grid every 32 voxels; the CPU passes `|anchor|² − R²` in f64 for the 8 anchors a tile meets.

## Deferred
Leven's **separate seam mesh** per block (re-mesh only the seam when a neighbour changes) needs a second mesh per block, i.e. 2 entities per block, until #1991 makes the blocks GPU instances of one entity. It is an optimisation on top of #1991, not a correctness fix: step 3 already closes the measured cause.

## Acceptance
- [x] QEF vertex, WGSL validates (`both_passes_validate`).
- [x] Touching leaves ≤ 1 level apart (`touching_leaves_are_balanced`).
- [x] Same-level meshes close (`a_meshed_sphere_is_watertight`).
- [ ] Smoke: flying in and out of a planet shows no cracks between blocks of different level (#1979).


## Research 2 (2026-11-23): meshing, seams and LOD at planet scale
Trigger: the transactional swap measured 43 ms CPU (8 passes, 5511 staged) on `earth_test`; the user asked what shipped projects do at very large distances.
Searched: Zylann voxel-tools docs, Lengyel Transvoxel (`transvoxel` crate), Gildea/Leven, legalian (DC + skirts), Joris Rijsdijk (surface nets planets, MIT), draquel/VoxelWorlds (UE5, GPU density, DC, planets ≤1000 km), bonsairobo building-blocks #26, Dupuy/Benyoub CBT (Intel, Earth-size planet on GPU), Aokana (GPU SVDAG), BinocMesher, Nanite/meshoptimizer cluster LOD.
Findings:
- **LOD rule**: everyone uses distance shells/bands where a block's resolution is constant relative to its distance (Zylann `lod_distance`, Joris `⌈log2(d / 2R)⌉`, VoxelWorlds bands + hysteresis + 2:1). Ours targets 1 voxel = 1 px, far finer than any of them (#1993).
- **Seams**, three schools: Transvoxel (MC only, neighbour LOD mask, visible steps); skirts (cheap, but z-fighting, cave and self-shadow artefacts reported); **seam ownership** (Leven, VoxelWorlds): a block's interior mesh has no vertex in its +x/+y/+z border cells and never re-meshes for a neighbour; one seam job per shared face/edge/corner reads both sides and is the only thing re-run on a neighbour LOD change. A new interior is held hidden until its seams land (capped, 1 s) and swaps with a dither crossfade (0.25–0.35 s).
- **Far field**: no project meshes voxels all the way to orbit. VoxelWorlds draws voxels only inside a window and, past it, the analytic surface on six cube-face quadtrees split by screen error; above an altitude the voxels unload. CBT does the far-field tessellation entirely on the GPU (Earth-size, < 0.2 ms).
- **Nanite**: a cluster DAG needs an offline simplification per mesh; no shipped planet builds it at runtime. Our meshlets package each block, they do not choose detail.
- `transvoxel` crate: CPU marching cubes. Rejected, since we mesh DC on the GPU. VoxelWorlds has no licence file: read only.
**Verdict: STUDY** — seam ownership as VoxelWorlds/Leven describe it, distance-shell LOD, and an analytic far field past a voxel window. The transactional swap (step 3 above) is the wrong design: it keeps meshes dependent on neighbours and costs CPU per frame. Separate seam meshes need #1991 (blocks as instances) first.


## Finding (2026-11-24): the steady-state holes are an edge seam nobody emits
`a_split_sphere_is_watertight` (branch `393-seam-ownership`) splits octants of a test sphere. One octant split, on the − or + side: **closed**. Three of the four around an axis split, or seven of eight: **1–2 open edges each**, all on the coarse block's edge where three fine blocks meet it (`L1 --.`), the dots seen in-game where 3–4 blocks meet.
Cause: the grid edge on that line has three fine cells and one coarse. The coarse block emits nothing touching a finer leaf; each fine block sees a same-level fine cell past its + plane, which `owns()` refuses, so no block emits it. No fine block could anyway: the fourth fine cell is past its 18-sample tile (it needs sample 18).
Fix: the one fine block whose start lies on its + planes toward the coarse leaf emits the edge, reading the fine neighbours' cells from their tiles, which `Near` records as same-level slots only on those directions.
